# PitchViva: final business direction

Decision: a community-led competition preparation service, supported by a free software workspace. Verified event information is an operating asset. Standalone Data as a Service is a later hypothesis, not a second product being launched now.

## First offer

A proposed four-week, ₹499-per-participant pilot. Initial focus: students preparing a project for one selected competition or a tightly related group of events. No subscription, winning guarantee, unlimited reviews, or unbounded mentor access.

Proposed delivery: an official-source event shortlist, one preparation session per week, structured peer feedback, optional team introductions, and one scoped submission review per team. Hosts, schedule, capacity, review limits, total payable price and cancellation terms must be settled before enrollment opens. The website currently accepts no application, payment or booking.

## Acquisition and delivery experiment

Start with one college or innovation cell. Interview interested students and the coordinator, show a sample event brief and review rubric, and establish delivery capacity before advertising seats. Run the actual pilot on a communication platform the host can moderate; do not build chat infrastructure first. Publish conduct, privacy, reporting and moderation procedures before inviting members.

The software handles individual preparation: requirements, evidence, pitch text, speaking plan, demo fallback and exports. Personal calendar downloads are reminders only. There is no shared membership system, attendance tracking, chat, reviewer assignment or cloud synchronization in the current app.

## What to measure

Track invited, interested, paid, attended, reviewed and submitted counts separately. Define a qualifying submission before the pilot. Record review time, support time, acquisition spending, refunds, delivery costs and participant feedback. Ask whether students would choose another cohort at the same price. Do not substitute signups or chat-message counts for delivered value.

Illustration, not a forecast: 20 participants at ₹499 gives ₹9,980 in gross receipts before taxes, payment fees, refunds, acquisition and delivery costs. This is not profit. Capacity should follow the time needed to deliver the promised reviews, not the largest possible group.

## Event data standard

Every event fact needs the official source URL, edition/track, date checked, reviewer and status. Deadlines need time zones. Eligibility, required files and AI policies must stay unknown when not supported. Recheck selected-event facts near deadlines and notify participants of material changes. An encyclopedia page is background, not official verification.

The current catalog has four references and a Wikipedia lookup; it does not meet this proposed paid data standard. A manually checked pilot shortlist is required before launch. Respect source access and reuse terms. Do not resell student drafts, member lists or personal information.

## Later business options

First test college-sponsored preparation cohorts. Only consider a standalone event-data feed after organizations ask for recurring data delivery and the team can measure coverage, freshness, accuracy and cost. Do not build an API or claim a data moat solely from public event listings.

## Immediate owner decisions

1. Name the host and reviewers; confirm available hours.
2. Select the event/college and publish the actual delivery dates.
3. Choose a contact channel and moderated community venue.
4. Confirm total price, review scope, turnaround and cancellation terms.
5. Configure enrollment and payment services, then test complete booking, receipt, reconciliation and cancellation paths.

Until those decisions and integrations are complete, the website remains a free workspace and planned-pilot page.
